readings: Worthy of the kingdom for which you suffer
Lord, let our eyes be opened
2027-05-18.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe), the seven weeks that begin at Pentecost. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari; from Pentecost “The Angel of the Lord” (the Angelus) is prayed again in place of the Queen of Heaven. In the Latin calendar today: St John I, pope and martyr (optional memorial).
2027-05-18.verse: Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes. Immediately they regained their sight and followed him.
theo: Jesus is leaving Jericho, the last town before the climb to Jerusalem, where the Cross awaits him. A large crowd follows him, and by the roadside sit two blind men. They cannot see him, but they hear that he is passing by, and they cry out: “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!” The crowd, perhaps embarrassed, perhaps impatient, tells them to be quiet. “But they shouted even more loudly, ‘Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!’” Their prayer is short, repeated, and stubborn. It is the prayer the Church has never stopped praying: in our Holy Qurbana and in the Prayer of the Hours we say again and again, Lord, have mercy; the Christian East has made of it the Jesus Prayer, repeated with every breath. There is always a crowd that tells us to be quiet: the voice of shame, of busyness, of people who think prayer is useless. The blind men teach us to cry louder. And notice what happens next: “Jesus stood still.” The One who has set his face towards Jerusalem stops for two beggars. No one is too small to halt the Lord on his way.

“What do you want me to do for you?” Jesus knows what they need, yet he asks. He wants them to say it, to name their deepest desire. “Lord, let our eyes be opened.” Matthew gives the reason for what follows in one phrase: “Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes.” The word for compassion is the one Matthew uses when Jesus sees the crowds like sheep without a shepherd: a love that moves the depths of the heart. He does not heal from a distance; he touches. “Immediately they regained their sight and followed him.” They do not go home to enjoy their new sight; they follow him on the road that leads to Jerusalem, to the Cross and to the Resurrection. In this first week of the Season of the Apostles, the Gospel shows us what the apostles became: people whose eyes had been opened by Jesus and who followed him wherever he went. Isaiah had said that the Servant would come “to open the eyes that are blind” (Isaiah 42:7). Every Baptism, which the ancient Church called illumination, is such an opening of the eyes; every confession and every Qurbana can be another touch of the Lord's compassion.

Paul writes to the young Church of Thessalonica with a pastor's pride: “your faith is growing abundantly, and the love of every one of you for one another is increasing.” They are suffering persecution, and he does not hide it, but he sees their “steadfastness and faith during all your persecutions and the afflictions that you are enduring” as a sign that God is making them “worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you are also suffering.” The strong language about God's judgment that follows is not a call to revenge; it is the assurance that God sees, that injustice will not have the last word, and that the Lord Jesus will be revealed “to be glorified by his saints and to be marveled at on that day among all who have believed.” Christians in many places, and in our own country, have known such afflictions; the faithful of Kandhamal in Odisha in 2008 are still remembered. Paul's answer to suffering is prayer: “To this end we always pray for you, asking that our God will make you worthy of his call and will fulfill by his power every good resolve and work of faith, so that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in him”. Faith that grows, love that increases, steadfastness under trial, and a prayer for one another: this is the portrait of an apostolic Church.
outline: Two blind men by the road out of Jericho, and the crowd that says, Be quiet.
Point 1 · Lord, have mercy on us
The stubborn prayer, and the Lord who stands still.
Point 2 · What do you want me to do for you?
Compassion that touches, and eyes opened to follow.
Faith growing, love increasing, steadfast under trial.
live: Pray the Jesus Prayer slowly ten times today: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me a sinner.
Pray today for Christians who suffer for their faith in India and elsewhere, and for those who make them suffer.
fathers: The crowd that tried to silence the blind men is the noise of our bad habits and of those who mock the life of prayer. When Christ passes by, let us cry out all the more, and he will stand still and give us light.

See their gratitude: once their eyes were opened, they did not leave him but followed him. They had asked for nothing small, not money or bread, but sight; and having received it, they gave him back their whole life.
magis: Jesus hears the prayer of faith; the urgent request of the blind men, “Have mercy on us, Son of David,” has been renewed in the traditional prayer to Jesus known as the Jesus Prayer.
Christ's compassion toward the sick and his many healings are a resplendent sign that God has visited his people; he often touches those he heals.
The invocation of the holy name of Jesus, “Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on us sinners,” can be repeated in every circumstance and keeps us in the presence of God.
2027-05-18.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of David, you stood still on the road for two blind beggars and opened their eyes with the touch of your compassion. Have mercy on us. Open the eyes of our hearts to see you, and let us follow you on the road you walk. Make our faith grow and our love for one another increase; keep steadfast all who suffer for your name, and make us worthy of your call, that your name may be glorified in us. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we pray, Lord, have mercy, like the blind men of Jericho. And the Lord stands still among us, touches us in his Body and Blood, and opens our eyes to recognise him and to follow him.

quick: Two blind men cry out, Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David, and shout louder when silenced.
Jesus stands still, asks what they want, is moved with compassion and touches their eyes; they follow him.
Paul: your faith is growing and your love increasing; may God make you worthy of his call.
2027-05-18.action: Pray the Jesus Prayer ten times today, slowly, especially when you feel discouraged.
2027-05-18.question: What is the blindness I most need Jesus to heal, and am I ready to follow him when he does?

family.explain: Two blind men were sitting by the road when Jesus was passing. They shouted, “Lord, have mercy on us!” People told them to keep quiet, but they shouted even louder. Jesus stopped, called them and asked, “What do you want me to do for you?” They said, “Lord, let our eyes be opened.” Jesus felt great love for them, touched their eyes, and they could see! Then they walked with Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for people who are blind or have weak eyes, and for those who cannot yet see how much God loves them.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there something we want to ask Jesus for, as a family, like the blind men did?”

illus: A retired schoolteacher in Pala lost most of her sight to an illness of the eyes in her seventies. Her grandchildren expected her to become bitter; instead she learned the Jesus Prayer from a priest who visited her and began to pray it all day, on her rosary beads, while sitting on the veranda. Neighbours started to come and sit with her, first out of kindness, then because they found peace there. A young man struggling with drink came every evening for months. When he was finally sober, he told her, “Teacher, you cannot see me, but you were the first person who saw me as someone worth praying for.” She laughed and said, “Jesus stood still for blind people. I only learned to stand still with him.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on us. As we gather in your name, open the eyes of our hearts and touch us with your compassion. Amen.
share: They shouted even more loudly, “Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!” (Matthew 20:31). What voices try to silence my prayer?
What do you want me to do for you? (Matthew 20:32). What would I answer Jesus tonight?
Your faith is growing abundantly, and the love of every one of you for one another is increasing (2 Thessalonians 1:3). Where do I see faith and love growing in our community?
That our God will make you worthy of his call (2 Thessalonians 1:11). How is God calling me in this season?
pm.resp: Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that her eyes may be opened to see Christ and follow him.
For Christians who suffer persecution, that they may remain steadfast in faith and love.
For the blind and visually impaired, and for those who care for them.
For those whose hearts are blind through sin, addiction or despair, that the Lord may stand still and touch them.
For our prayer group, that our faith may grow and our love for one another increase.
pm.close: Father, your Son had compassion on the blind and opened their eyes. Open the eyes of our hearts, make us worthy of your call, and let us follow Jesus on his way. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Jesus is leaving Jericho on his way to Jerusalem and the Cross. Two blind men by the road hear that he is passing and cry out: “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!” (Matthew 20:30).

The crowd tells them to be quiet. But they shout even louder. There is always a crowd that tries to silence our prayer: shame, tiredness, people who say prayer is useless. Let us learn from the blind men to cry louder. Our liturgy repeats again and again, Lord, have mercy.

“Jesus stood still.” The Lord on his way to the Cross stops for two beggars. He asks, “What do you want me to do for you?” They say, “Lord, let our eyes be opened.” Moved with compassion, he touches their eyes, and they see, and they follow him (Matthew 20:32–34).

Paul praises the Thessalonians: their faith is growing and their love increasing, even under persecution. He prays that God will make them “worthy of his call” (2 Thessalonians 1:11). That is the portrait of the Church of the apostles: eyes opened, faith growing, love increasing, steadfast in trial.

In this Season of the Apostles let us cry to the Lord for mercy, tell him honestly what we need, and when he opens our eyes, follow him. Let us also pray for our brothers and sisters who suffer for their faith. Amen.
kids: Children, two blind men shouted to Jesus, “Lord, have mercy on us!” People said, “Be quiet!” but they shouted louder. Jesus stopped, touched their eyes, and they could see! Jesus always stops when we call him.

intro: Theme: “Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes. Immediately they regained their sight and followed him.”
The stubborn prayer of the blind, the compassion that touches and opens the eyes, and a Church made worthy of its call.

The crowd that says, Be quiet.
q: the LORD opens the eyes of the blind. The LORD lifts up those who are bowed down; the LORD loves the righteous.
When they heard that Jesus was passing by, they shouted, “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!”
points.apply: Pray the Jesus Prayer every day this week, morning and evening.

points.h: What do you want me to do for you?

Jesus stood still and called them, saying, “What do you want me to do for you?”
points.apply: Tell Jesus honestly, in a quiet moment, the one thing you most need from him.

q: The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases, his mercies never come to an end;
To this end we always pray for you, asking that our God will make you worthy of his call and will fulfill by his power every good resolve and work of faith,
points.apply: Pray by name this week for three people in your parish, that God may make them worthy of his call.

concl: The Lord who stood still for the blind of Jericho stands still for us, opens our eyes and calls us to follow.
Let us follow him with faith that grows and love that increases, steadfast in every trial.
2027-05-18.resolve: This week, pray the Jesus Prayer daily, name your need to the Lord, and pray for the persecuted and for your parish.
